text: THE REVIEW MATERIAL CUTS BY PATH ORDER, NOT RELEVANCE — measured 2026-09-26 on 12/11-implementation-decision-record, from the worker own F8. `buildReviewMaterial` cuts the diff at DIFF_CHARS=60000 (after excluding .ann/journey), and the cut is a flat prefix in path order, so src/surface/* sorts late and falls off the end. The documented mitigation is real and is why this is not a violated AC: the change map above the patch is complete and the cut length is written inline, so a file whose hunks were cut is always NAMED. But naming the loss cannot stop a criterion becoming UNVERIFIABLE. Numbers from the run: the assembled prompt was 80,267 chars; the cut dropped 30,370 chars of diff; the lost hunks included src/surface/ui.ts (+16) and src/surface/handlers.ts (+6), which is exactly where AC-1 (the SERVED CARD confirm form asks before it writes) would be settled. The model raised F8 [uncertain], naming the two files and the hunks it needed, and the rule correctly routed the run to the human with no rejection burned. CONCLUSION: the barrier is NOT a missing agent loop — one pass walked all five ACs and said what it needed. The fix is deterministic material selection: the hunks of the files the claims and ACs name go in FIRST, then the diff truncates.
